correctness.rationale: On the critical line, the symmetric part of the interaction matrix is the all-ones matrix, so S'=S(1−S) and the normalized competition is antisymmetric. Positive solutions exist globally for locally integrable rates: the positive orthant is invariant, each coordinate has a scalar Grönwall lower bound on finite intervals, and S bounds the populations. Direct differentiation of H gives −μD with D=(Σ1/p_i−9)/3. For x=3p_i, 1/x−1+log x≥0 gives D≥3H. The sublevel H≤H(0) is compact in the open simplex, and D/H extends to 6 at u by the quadratic terms 9Σ(p_i−1/3)² and (3/2)Σ(p_i−1/3)². Boundedness of the extended ratio and integration give a positive lower bound if M is finite, and no finite-time hit of u. Infinite M forces H→0, and averaging the extended ratio with weights dM gives the limit −6. For finite M, the positive limiting entropy level is one smooth closed curve by strict convexity, and the unmutated tangent field is nowhere zero there because α≠1. On any bounded translated time window ∫μ tends to zero, even with unbounded pulses, while S→1 uniformly. Continuous dependence via the integral equation then puts the full forward unmutated orbit through any accumulation point into the omega-limit set. This is the whole level; S→1 transfers it to densities. Integrating the example schedule gives the stated cutoff and q=1 exponent.

value.rationale: This identifies the scalar budget separating convergence from persistence of cycling in a standard critical competition model even when the rate is pulsed or lacks a limit. It quantifies the infinite-budget branch sharply in its natural clock and identifies the full limit set in the finite-budget branch rather than just precluding convergence. The constant-rate observation alone would not justify this value.
